rationale: The question is how well a deployed index test (the flag) classifies a target condition (boarding of four hours or more) against a reference standard, which is a diagnostic accuracy design applied to a prognostic flag. The log of every score since March 2025 allows a consecutive series with complete verification by timestamps, avoiding partial verification bias. External validation of a similar tool (c1), calibration loss at external sites (c2), reference standard error (c3) and spectrum effects (c4) shape the protocol.
alternatives: Before-after comparison of boarding hours around the command centre opening (refused: it would not show whether the flag identifies the right patients)
Development of a new local model (refused: the score cannot be changed during the evaluation; a model could follow the evaluation)
Cluster randomised trial of flag display (refused: one command centre and no research funding)
whyNotMoreComplex: A randomised evaluation of escalation would answer a different question and needs several hospitals; an accuracy study of the deployed flag uses existing logs and answers the command centre's question.

decision.statement: Evaluate the accuracy of the deployed boarding-risk flag against observed boarding of four hours or more, using the score log and a documented timestamp reference standard from March 2025 to February 2027, and report sensitivity, specificity and calibration by time of day, weekday and admitting service.
decision.question: Does the command centre flag identify the admitted patients who will board for four hours or more?

criteria.text: Published tools of this kind show moderate and uneven accuracy, so local performance cannot be assumed.
The reference standard cannot be measured reliably from local timestamps.

gates.requirement: Data governance approval for command centre logs and emergency timestamps
gates.evidence: Approval DG-2026-311 dated 2026-08-28, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Analyst time for data extraction and analysis
gates.evidence: Command centre analyst one day a week until June 2027, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Development of a new local model after the evaluation
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c4 from retrieved records; none of the four model leads is cited, including the vendor's own report.

summary: Diagnostic accuracy study of the deployed flag recommended; both gates met.
